transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

I'm just... having some trouble keeping things together at work. I guess I'm here because I can't seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. There are patent notes, workshop prep, deadlines, team decisions... and I just end up starting whatever is loudest instead of what actually matters. It's getting to be a problem.
Have you always had difficulty organizing tasks and prioritizing what's important, or is this something that's gotten worse recently?

I suppose it's... always been there, really. It's not just a recent thing. Even back in grade school, I remember... well, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but that I daydreamed a lot. I'd actually finish my assignments and then just... forget to turn them in. Or I'd lose my homework folders entirely. That was all long before I even hit my teens. So, yeah... it's been a while.
Besides the trouble organizing and prioritizing, do you find yourself fidgeting a lot, feeling restless, or having difficulty sitting still for extended periods?

I don't know if I'd call it fidgeting, really. But... I guess sitting still can be hard sometimes. 

Like, if I'm on a long design call, I start to feel this... pressure building up in my body to just get up. So I usually end up pacing around my office. Or shifting from chair to chair... even when I'm just trying to look focused on the screen. So, I suppose I do get restless.

When you were a child and teenager, before you started working, would you say you felt generally okay emotionally? Or did you notice periods where you felt persistently sad, down, or anxious even back then?
I... no, I think I was mostly fine. I don't really remember feeling down or anxious back then. Just... a normal kid, I guess. I didn't really have any problems with that.
